acme-sre: Hey team — we've got Vercel Edge function calls to the Redwood hosted API failing with CORS preflight. Works locally (curl) but browser shows OPTIONS 403 and 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' missing. Blocking prod rollout.

acme-sre: Minimal repro: Vercel edge function imports the TS SDK and proxies requests from the browser. When the browser hits our edge route, console shows: 

```
Access to fetch at 'https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/responses' from origin 'https://app.acme.com' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.
```

jess-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the edge function code and the SDK version? Also are you shipping the API key to the browser?

acme-sre: SDK is `@redwood-inference/sdk@0.10.0`. Edge function (simplified):

```
import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
export default async (req) => {
  const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const body = await req.json();
  const res = await client.responses.create({ model: 'redwood/fast-1', input: body.prompt });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(res), { status: 200 });
};
```

acme-sre: We only call this from the browser (fetch('/api/infer', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({prompt}) })), so the browser does an OPTIONS then POST. OPTIONS returns 403 from the Redwood API. curl to the edge route returns 200.

jess-support: Two quick checks: 1) confirm the browser request isn't sending the Redwood API key from the client bundle; 2) can you paste the raw network request/response (headers) for the preflight?

acme-sre: Here's the preflight request headers we see in the browser:

```
OPTIONS /v1/responses HTTP/1.1
Origin: https://app.acme.com
Access-Control-Request-Method: POST
Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type, authorization
```

And response: `403 Forbidden` with no CORS headers.

nate-devex: Root cause is likely that your browser is talking directly to `api.redwood-inference.example` (or it's being proxied incorrectly) — the preflight goes to Redwood, not your Vercel edge. If your edge function is properly proxying, the browser should hit your domain (no cross-origin). Are you returning CORS headers from the edge route?

acme-sre: The browser calls our edge route at `https://app.acme.com/api/infer`. That route then calls Redwood's API server-side. But the network tab shows the OPTIONS going to `api.redwood-inference.example` (not our domain). So something in our code is redirecting/pointing browser to Redwood directly.

jess-support: Two common ways this happens: a) SDK is being bundled into the client bundle (so client code is calling Redwood directly), or b) your fetch from the browser is pointing to the wrong URL. Can you confirm the edge route code is actually running and not being inlined in the client?

acme-sre: Hmm we do SSR + an API file in `pages/api/infer.ts` which should be server. But we use a shared helper `lib/infer.ts` that imports the SDK — and we accidentally import `lib/infer` from a client-side React component for local dev. Our bundler pulled the SDK into the browser bundle. So the browser is calling Redwood directly with the API key baked in for dev — oops.

omar-eng-runtime: That explains CORS + auth risk. Two notes: 1) We intentionally reject requests that present an Authorization header from a browser origin for hosted API keys — to prevent leaky API keys being used from client-side (this triggers 403 preflight in your case). 2) For edge runtimes like Vercel Edge/CF Workers, use the `edge` entrypoint of the SDK or keep the SDK server-only. SDK 0.10.0's default build may be Node-targeted and can be accidentally bundled.

nate-devex: Workarounds:
- Ensure the SDK is only imported in server-only code (do not import from client bundles).
- If you must call from edge runtime, use the edge-optimized import: `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk/edge'` (newer SDKs provide an explicit edge/browser-safe entry).
- Rotate the API key immediately if it was bundled into client builds.

acme-sre: OK that matches. We found `import { infer } from '../lib/infer'` in a component — that pulled the helper into the client. We rotated the key. After removing the import, the browser no longer directly calls Redwood. But we still saw one failing case in prod where Vercel Edge route returned 502 / CORS missing when proxying.

jess-support: Can you paste the Vercel Edge function response headers (the proxied response to browser)? If your edge route proxies Redwood's response, you must forward CORS headers back to the browser. In Vercel Edge you typically return: `new Response(body, { headers: { 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': origin, 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials': 'true' }})` for preflight/OPTIONS handling.

acme-sre: We weren't handling OPTIONS in the edge function — Vercel auto-handles some things but not the preflight when proxied. Quick fix: add an explicit handler for OPTIONS that returns the proper headers, and ensure the POST response includes `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` too.

```
if (req.method === 'OPTIONS') {
  return new Response(null, {
    status: 204,
    headers: {
      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': req.headers.get('origin') || '*',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': 'POST, OPTIONS',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Content-Type, Authorization',
    },
  });
}
```

nate-devex: Also check your bundler: upgrades to Vite/Next can cause server-only imports to be included in client builds if the import graph isn't SSR-safe. Prefer dynamic `await import()` inside server-only functions or keep SDK imports in `pages/api`/`app/api` files only.

acme-sre: After removing client import and adding the OPTIONS handler, things look good in staging. Quick question: Is there an official recommended pattern for Vercel Edge + Redwood API?

omar-eng-runtime: Yes — recommended patterns:
- For browser-to-Redwood: don't call Redwood directly from browser. Use a server-side proxy/edge function that holds the API key.
- For Vercel Edge specifically: use `@redwood-inference/sdk/edge` if you need to run in the Edge Runtime and hold secrets there. Ensure your edge function explicitly handles OPTIONS and copies CORS headers from Redwood responses, or sets them explicitly for the browser.
- Avoid shipping `Authorization` or long-lived keys in client bundles — rotate keys if exposed.

jess-support: Also note SDK version advice: we fixed a bundling/exports issue in `@redwood-inference/sdk@0.11.2` that makes the `edge` entrypoint explicit and gives clearer ESM/exports to avoid bundlers accidentally pulling server code into client bundles. If anyone is on 0.10.x and sees weird bundle behavior, upgrade.

acme-sre: Thanks — we'll upgrade SDK in our monorepo and patch the import graph. Big thanks for the quick help.

deploy-bot: Canary for `web@release/2026-03-15` deployed to production regions. :rocket:

jess-support: Follow-up checklist for support: 1) confirm key rotation done, 2) confirm no client bundles contain SDK, 3) confirm edge function handles OPTIONS and sets CORS headers, 4) recommend SDK upgrade to 0.11.2+ if running into bundling issues.

acme-sre: Checklist done. Marking fixed on our side. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:
